title: Superconductivity in High-Entropy Alloy System Containing Tb.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A bcc high-entropy alloy based on refractory elements (e.g., Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–Ti) with partial substitution by Tb to form Tb_x(TaNbHfZrTi)_{1−x} arc-melted polycrystalline ingots.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Systematic incorporation of magnetic Tb at various atomic percentages into the HEA matrix via arc melting (and possible annealing), followed by structural (XRD/EDX) and physical property measurements (resistivity, magnetization, heat capacity) to track superconductivity versus Tb content.
recollection.structure: Guess: Predominantly single-phase bcc random solid solution retained up to about 10–15 at.% Tb; beyond that, minor secondary phases appear. Microstructure is polycrystalline with fairly homogeneous Tb distribution.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Conventional dirty-limit s-wave BCS superconductivity inherited from the parent refractory HEA, with magnetic pair-breaking from localized Tb 4f moments. Tc suppression follows Abrikosov–Gor'kov behavior; normal-state magnetism shows Curie–Weiss paramagnetism and possible low-temperature spin-glass-like freezing competing with superconductivity.
recollection.results: Guess: Parent HEA Tc0 ≈ 7–8 K; Tc decreases with Tb content: ≈6 K at ~5 at.% Tb, ≈3–4 K at ~10 at.% Tb, and superconductivity vanishes near ~15 at.% Tb. Bulk superconductivity evidenced by a heat-capacity jump ΔC/γTc ≈ 1.3–1.5; upper critical field μ0Hc2(0) ≈ 6–10 T; high residual resistivity (~100–200 μΩ·cm). Magnetic analysis gives μ_eff per Tb ≈ 9–10 μB with a small negative Curie–Weiss θ (≈−5 to −20 K). Data fit an Abrikosov–Gor'kov pair-breaking trend consistent with magnetic scattering.

score.note: The recollection correctly gestures toward arc-melted Tb incorporation into a refractory bcc HEA, but invents a concentration series and misidentifies the parent composition. It recognizes a bcc matrix and possible secondary phases, yet incorrectly describes Tb as homogeneous and misses the quantified Tb/Tb2O3 inclusions. The proposed Abrikosov–Gor'kov magnetic pair-breaking and spin-glass mechanism is unsupported and contradicts the paper's stated uncertainty and lack of magnetic ordering. Some broad Hc2 and heat-capacity-jump estimates overlap the measurements, but the Tc values and claimed dose-dependent suppression are substantially wrong.
